messages:
jess_support: FYI Kudo Health is hitting sporadic JSON.parse errors when using JSON mode on /v1/generate. They see concatenated objects and occasionally fields from different responses mixed together. Sample attached.

customer_kudo: Example from our consumer logs (redacted):\n```\n{"record":{"id":42,"name":"Bob"}}{"meta":{"source":"device-a"}}\n```\nSometimes we also get embedded fields like `\"note\":\"BP normal\"` landing inside the wrong object.

jess_support: Request we received from customer: POST /v1/generate with payload: \n```\n{\n  \"model\": \"open-redwood-1\",\n  \"input\": \"emit patient record json\",\n  \"json_mode\": true,\n  \"batch_size\": 12,\n  \"stream\": false,\n  \"kv_cache\": \"enabled\",\n  \"prefetch\": true\n}\n```\nThey see failure rate ~0.2-0.5% but spikes under burst load.

alex_runtime: Thanks. Initial triage: this smells like an assembly buffer race where multiple response fragments are appended without a clear delimiter when prefetch is enabled and multiple shards/threads write to a shared output region. Prefetch + batching + warm KV cache are common preconditions in our internal repros.

sam_sre: Can you share request ids/times so I can pull router + worker logs? Also any recent runtime deploys?

jess_support: Provided IDs: req_X9A1B2 (primary), req_X9A1B3 (same minute). Occurred ~2026-03-10T17:03:45Z. Deploy-bot shows eng-runtime v2026.3.9 (change 3445) deployed ~2026-03-10T16:50Z.

deploy-bot: rollout complete for eng-runtime v2026.3.9 (change 3445) at 2026-03-10T16:50:02Z.

kudo_ci_bot: Customer attached reproducible artifacts in support-1012 (repro script + sample outputs). They can run a canary patch if provided.

alex_runtime: Reproducer we ran: 16 parallel clients, batch_size=12, prefetch=true, seed same prefix to warm KV cache. After ~2000 requests we observed concatenated objects in ~0.3% of responses. Repro steps attached to internal bug 4827.

marta_account: Kudo Health requests a mitigation: either a quick patch or allow us to toggle prefetch per-tenant. They're losing nightly jobs and performing retries which inflate billing.

alex_runtime: Short-term mitigations:
- A: advise customer to set prefetch=false or batch_size=1 (serviceable but costly throughput-wise).
- B: add defensive flush/boundary markers at response assembly when json_mode=true (small latency/regression risk but quick).
- C: if root cause ties to change 3445, consider targeted rollback.

sam_sre: I'm pulling worker logs for req_X9A1B2 now and will grep for "assemble_output" and buffer offsets. Will post traces in this thread.

jess_support: Customer willing to test a canary in us-west-2. They prefer a patch over disabling features. Can we get a same-day canary?

alex_runtime: I'll prototype a minimal guard that ensures a buffer flush and boundary verification for JSON mode. If tests pass, we can push a canary today to a small fleet. Risk: adds ~5-12ms to tail latency in some cases.

marta_account: I'll offer a billing credit for retry costs and coordinate validation with the customer's SREs. Please tag me when canary is up.

alex_runtime: Action items assigned: @sam_sre collect and upload logs for req_X9A1B2/3 (P0). @alex_runtime implement guard + unit test (P0). @eng-ml create regression test that simulates concurrent assembly (P1). @jess_support coordinate canary with customer and get validation (P0).

customer_kudo: Thanks. We'll stand by for canary details. Also please include a config knob to disable prefetch at tenant-level as fallback.

jess_support: Noted. Adding tenant prefetch toggle request to the feature backlog and will escalate for short-term flag if needed.

sam_sre: Log pull complete for req_X9A1B2. Evidence: two worker threads wrote offsets that overlapped by 128 bytes before flush; attaching trace snippet. Posting in internal bug 4827.

alex_runtime: Good catch. That confirms buffer reuse without atomic boundary handling. I'll submit a small PR that acquires a per-response assembly lock when json_mode=true and forces a flush boundary. Will coordinate canary rollout after CI.

jess_support: Thank you team. Updating support ticket and will notify customer once canary URL is ready. :thumbsup:
